notes: I-JSON is a restricted profile of JSON for Internet protocols. It is not a fourth JSON grammar; it constrains how JSON is used.

cases.title: I-JSON messages should be objects (or arrays)
cases.paragraph: An I-JSON message can be any JSON value. However, older RFC 4627 implementations only accept objects or arrays at the top level; protocols are advised to use an object or array.

cases.title: I-JSON text is UTF-8
cases.paragraph: I-JSON messages MUST be encoded using UTF-8.

cases.title: I-JSON forbids unpaired surrogates
cases.paragraph: I-JSON messages MUST NOT include characters or escape sequences that represent unpaired UTF-16 surrogates or noncharacter code points.

cases.title: I-JSON objects MUST have unique member names
cases.paragraph: Objects in I-JSON messages MUST have unique member names.
cases.notes: Most JSON parsers accept this and keep one value. That is an I-JSON profile miss, not an RFC 8259 grammar miss.

cases.title: Numbers should be IEEE 754 binary64
cases.paragraph: I-JSON messages SHOULD NOT include numbers that look like integers but cannot be represented as an IEEE 754-2008 binary64 value without loss.
cases.notes: 2^53+1 is not exactly representable in binary64. Parsers that silently coerce to 9007199254740992 lose an I-JSON guarantee.

cases.title: NaN is outside I-JSON (and JSON)
cases.paragraph: I-JSON is a profile of JSON; NaN is not a JSON number.
